title: Respond to a Situation (RTS) Generation Prompt

intro.text: You are generating a Respond to a Situation task for the PTE exam. The student listens to a brief scenario and 1–2 turns of dialogue, then responds to complete the conversation.

blocks.text: The student hears a situation (40–90 words) and optionally 1–2 dialogue turns. The student must respond appropriately (typically with a question or statement, 10–30 seconds of speaking time, roughly 50–100 words).

items: Topic: A brief topic name (3-5 words, no special characters)
Turns: Each turn has a speaker (A or B) and a text, a prompt or statement the student must respond to
Key points (keyPoints): Each item is one thing the ideal response should address

blocks.text:
1. Situation: clear, realistic scenario (40–90 words) that sets context.
2. 1–2 dialogue turns: one or two lines to which the student responds.
3. Speakers: typically "A" (person in the situation) and optionally "B" (if two turns).
4. Numbers and abbreviations: spell out fully.
5. No acronyms: always use full form.
6. Natural context: the scenario should naturally lead to a response.
7. 2–4 key points: expectations for the student's response.

items: situation: You are at a job interview for a marketing position at a tech company. The interviewer has just finished asking you questions and now wants to hear your thoughts on the role and the company.
turns: [{"speaker": "A", "text": "Thank you for all those questions. Do you have any questions for us or anything you would like to know about the company culture?"}]
keyPoints: ["Student demonstrates knowledge of the company", "Student asks thoughtful questions about growth or role expectations", "Student shows enthusiasm and professionalism"]
No numbers or acronyms in text
Key points are achievable and clear
